target.title: refactor: use `node:timers/promises` setTimeout in managed-service handoff script
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes a hand-written `sleep(ms)` helper in the managed-service update handoff CJS script that re-implements what `node:timers/promises` already provides. The stdlib version has been available since Node.js 16 and OpenClaw already uses it across the codebase (see `src/gateway/`, `src/agents/`, etc.).

## Why This Change Was Made

The handoff script (`HANDOFF_SCRIPT` string literal written to `handoff.cjs`) had its own `sleep` function:
```js
function sleep(ms) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}
```

This is functionally identical to `const { setTimeout: sleep } = require("node:timers/promises")` but adds unnecessary code that a reviewer has to read and potentially audit. Using the stdlib version is the idiomatic approach and consistent with the rest of the codebase. The change is 1 line added, 3 lines removed.

## User Impact

None. Zero behavioral change.

## Evidence

All existing tests pass:

```
$ pnpm test -- src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```
